heading: CommonJS modules
body:
### `require(specifier[, options])`

Used to import JavaScript or JSON modules and local files. Relative paths such as `./`, `./foo`, `./bar/baz`, and `../foo` are resolved against the directory named by `__dirname`. POSIX-style paths are resolved in an OS-independent fashion, so the same relative paths work on Windows as they do on POSIX systems.

Returns the exported module contents.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `specifier` | `string` | — | The module specifier to resolve and load. |
| `options?` | [`RequireOptions`](#requireoptions) | — | Options for the call; `with.type` selects how the file should be loaded — one of `'script'`, `'module'`, `'json'`, `'bundle'`, `'addon'`, `'binary'`, or `'text'` (see [`Module.constants`](#moduleconstants)). A `type` that is not one of these is turned down rather than passed over, as is a `type` that is not a string. `with.imports` names an `"imports"` map to apply to the module and its dependencies, `with.host` selects the WebAssembly build of their addons, and `with.wasi` names its WASI provider (see [WebAssembly addons](#webassembly-addons)). |

### `require.main`

The module representing the entry script where the program was launched.

### `require.cache`

The registry of loaded modules for this module's graph, keyed by URL `href`.

### `require.resolve(specifier[, parentURL][, options])`

Uses the internal machinery of `require()` to resolve `specifier` relative to the URL `parentURL` and returns the path string.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `specifier` | `string` | — | The module specifier to resolve. |
| `parentURL?` | `string` \| `URL` | the module's own URL | The URL to resolve `specifier` relative to. When it is passed, the resolutions are recorded for `parentURL` rather than the calling module, which is useful when resolving on behalf of another module. |
| `options?` | [`RequireOptions`](#requireoptions) | — | Added in v7.2.0. If `with` is passed, the graph of the resolved module is linked, but not evaluated, with the attributes applied, so that its resolutions are recorded in [`module.resolutions`](#resolutions-resolutionsmap). That lets the module be prepared later from its path alone, such as when spawning a thread with an imports map applied: `require.resolve('./worker.js', { with: { imports: './imports.json' } })`. |

### `require.addon([specifier][, parentURL])`

Also used to import modules, but loads only addon modules. `specifier` is resolved relative to `parentURL` using the [addon resolution](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-addon-resolve#algorithm) algorithm.

Returns the exported module contents.

A common pattern for writing an addon module is to use `require.addon()` as the JavaScript module's exports:

```js
module.exports = require.addon()
```

### `require.addon.host`

The platform and architecture used when resolving addons, following the pattern `<platform>-<arch>[-<environment>]`. The same value as `Bare.Addon.host`. The architecture can contain a `-`, such as `arm64-32` in `watchos-arm64-32`. Changed in v7.5.1: the loader splits the host into conditions with [`bare-host-parser`](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-host-parser), where it split it at every `-` before.

### `require.addon.resolve([specifier][, parentURL])`

Resolves `specifier` relative to `parentURL` as an addon and returns the path string, using the [addon resolution algorithm](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-addon-resolve#algorithm).

### `require.asset(specifier[, parentURL])`

Resolves `specifier` relative to `parentURL` and returns the path of the asset as a string. Can be used to load assets, for example to load `./foo.txt` from the local file system:

```js
const fs = require('bare-fs')
const contents = fs.readFileSync(require.asset('./foo.txt'))
```

heading: ECMAScript modules
body:
### `import defaultExport, * as name, { export1, export2 as alias2 } from 'specifier' with { type: 'json' }`

The static `import` declaration imports read-only live bindings that are exported by another module. The imported bindings are called _live_ bindings because they are updated by the module that exported the binding, but cannot be re-assigned by the importing module. For more on `import` syntax, see [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import).

The `with` clause takes the same [attributes](#attributes) as the `with` option of `require()`, including `host` and `wasi`:

```js
import { DatabaseSync } from 'bare-sqlite' with { host: 'wasi-wasm32', wasi: './wasi.js' }
```

### `import.meta.url`

The string representation of the URL for the current module.

### `import.meta.main`

A boolean representing whether the current module is the entry script where the program was launched.

### `import.meta.cache`

The registry of loaded modules for this module's graph, keyed by URL `href`. The same value as `require.cache` for a CommonJS module of the same graph.

### `import.meta.dirname`

The directory name of the current module.

### `import.meta.filename`

The file name of the current module.

### `import.meta.resolve(specifier[, parentURL][, options])`

A module-relative resolution function that returns the URL string for the module. `specifier` is a string resolved relative to `parentURL`, a WHATWG `URL`. `options` are the same as for [`require.resolve()`](#requireresolvespecifier-parenturl-options), and were added in v7.2.0.

### `import.meta.addon([specifier][, parentURL])`

Also used to import modules, but loads only addon modules. `specifier` is resolved relative to `parentURL` using the [addon resolution](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-addon-resolve#algorithm) algorithm.

Returns the exported module contents.

### `import.meta.addon.host`

The platform and architecture used when resolving addons, following the pattern `<platform>-<arch>[-<environment>]`. The same value as `Bare.Addon.host`. The architecture can contain a `-`, such as `arm64-32` in `watchos-arm64-32`. Changed in v7.5.1: the loader splits the host into conditions with [`bare-host-parser`](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-host-parser), where it split it at every `-` before.

### `import.meta.addon.resolve([specifier][, parentURL])`

Resolves `specifier` relative to `parentURL` as an addon and returns the URL string, using the [addon resolution algorithm](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-addon-resolve#algorithm).

### `import.meta.asset(specifier[, parentURL])`

Resolves `specifier` relative to `parentURL` and returns the URL of the asset as a string.

heading: WebAssembly addons
body:
Added in v7.5.0, which ships with Bare 1.36.0. An addon package can ship a WebAssembly build, `prebuilds/wasi-wasm32/<name>.wasm`, next to its native prebuilds. The loader runs it through [`bare-wasm-abi`](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-wasm-abi), sandboxed by [`bare-wasi`](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-wasi): through WASI, the addon reaches only what its WASI provider grants. It still reaches whatever JavaScript in its realm can, because the ABI hands it the global object. Changed in v7.5.2: WebAssembly addons are not supported on FreeRTOS. There, the loader doesn't load `bare-wasm-abi`, and evaluating a `.wasm` addon throws `ADDON_HOST_INCOMPATIBLE` with the message `WebAssembly addons are not supported on this platform`.

### Loading an addon as WebAssembly

The `host` attribute asks for the WebAssembly build of the addons of a module and everything it imports. The `wasi` attribute names the WASI provider for them:

```js
const { DatabaseSync } = require('bare-sqlite', {
  with: { host: 'wasi-wasm32', wasi: './wasi.js' }
})
```

`wasi-wasm32` is the only host the attribute accepts. A package with no `.wasm` build throws `ADDON_NOT_FOUND`. When the specifier is a string literal, write both attributes as string literals too: the import is linked before the module runs, using only the attributes written as literals, so a computed value conflicts with that link, and the call throws `ADDON_HOST_INCOMPATIBLE` or `ADDON_WASI_INCOMPATIBLE`. With a computed specifier, computed attributes work. With `host` set, the `wasi` and `wasm32` conditions of a package's `"exports"` and `"imports"` match alongside those of the native host, in the order the package lists them. Without it, they are tried only as a fallback, after the native conditions.

Without a `host` attribute, the loader uses the native build of an addon when one exists, and falls back to the `.wasm` build when there is no native prebuild or linked addon for the host. A fallback addon gets the provider of a `wasi` attribute on its import, which works without `host`, or else the loader's `wasi` option, which Bare doesn't set. With neither, WASI gives it no capabilities except clocks.

### WASI providers

A WASI provider is a module that exports a function, as `module.exports` or its default export. The loader calls it with the `URL` of each WebAssembly addon and passes what it returns to [`new WASI()`](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-wasi#wasi):

```js
// wasi.js
const { DirectorySync } = require('bare-directory')
const { HostDirectory } = require('bare-wasi/host')

module.exports = (url) => ({
  version: 'preview1',
  preopens: {
    '/': new HostDirectory(DirectorySync.open(__dirname + '/data'))
  }
})
```

The `wasi` specifier is resolved relative to the importing module and loaded like any other module. A provider that exports neither a function nor an object whose `default` is a function throws a `TypeError` when the addon is evaluated. A provider function that returns nothing, such as an arrow function with a block body, leaves the addon with the default options. The provider runs as application code, so install what it imports, such as `bare-wasi` and `bare-directory`: the copy of `bare-wasi` that Bare bundles for its loader can't be imported. Options without `version: 'preview1'` throw a `WASIError` with code `INVALID_VERSION`. An addon imported without a `wasi` attribute gets the options from the loader's [`wasi` option](#options), or only clocks through WASI.

The README of v7.5.0 to v7.5.2 shows a provider that grants randomness with `crypto.getRandomValues()`. Bare has no `crypto` global, so use `randomFillSync()` from [`bare-crypto`](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-crypto) instead.

### One context per package

The addons of a package load in one context per loader: the host and WASI provider it is first imported under. Importing it under another throws:

| Error code | Thrown when |
| --- | --- |
| `ADDON_HOST_INCOMPATIBLE` | A package's addons are already resolved for the default hosts and it is imported with `host`, or the other way round, or an addon below a `host` import is not WebAssembly. Also thrown, from `require.addon()` and catchable, as `Cannot resolve addon … which is linked in several contexts`, when one package's addons are reached both natively and with `host`, such as `bare-directory` imported with `host` while a provider loads it natively. |
| `ADDON_WASI_INCOMPATIBLE` | A package's WebAssembly addons already have one WASI provider and it is imported with another. On Bare 1.36, a dynamic `import()` with a `wasi` attribute also throws it, naming the same provider. |
| `UNKNOWN_ADDON_HOST` | A `host` attribute is not `wasi-wasm32`. |

These are thrown by [`bare-module-traverse`](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-module-traverse#the-host-and-wasi-import-attributes) while the importing module is linked, before any of its code runs, so a `try` block around a static `require()` doesn't catch them. A `require()` whose specifier the lexer can't read, such as a computed name, is linked when it runs, so these errors are thrown from that call and can be caught, and so are those from a computed attribute next to a string-literal specifier. A `require.resolve()` of the package counts as importing it with the default hosts. An `ADDON_NOT_FOUND` for a missing `.wasm` build is thrown when the module that loads the addon runs, and can be caught around a `require()` or `import()`, but not around a static `import` declaration.

On Bare 1.36, a dynamic `import()` doesn't apply its `wasi` attribute, because the runtime passes only the first import attribute to the loader. With a string-literal specifier, it throws `ADDON_WASI_INCOMPATIBLE`, naming the same provider. With a computed specifier, the addon loads with the default options. Pass a provider with `require()` or a static `import`, or use Bare 1.37.0 or later, which passes every attribute.

### After `Bare.Addon.seal()`

Once the process is [sealed](/bare/reference/bare/runtime#bareaddon), a native addon loads only if the process already loaded it, while WebAssembly addons still load. When resolving an addon on a sealed process, the loader skips native builds that `Bare.Addon.loaded()` reports as not loaded, so a package that also ships a `.wasm` build falls back to it, with the capabilities described above. This applies only to addons resolved after the seal. An addon reached through string-literal `require()` or `import()` specifiers from the module that calls `Bare.Addon.seal()`, or from any module linked with it before the seal, was resolved at link time, so its native addon throws `CANNOT_LOAD` even when the module that loads it runs after the seal. A package resolved after the seal that ships no `.wasm` build throws `ADDON_NOT_FOUND`, where Bare 1.35 threw `CANNOT_LOAD`. The provider's own native addons, such as `bare-directory` for a `HostDirectory`, follow the same rules, so load them before calling `Bare.Addon.seal()`, or the import fails. None of this applies inside a bundle: its modules keep the resolutions recorded at pack time, so after the seal a native addon the process hasn't loaded throws `CANNOT_LOAD`, even when the bundle also holds the `.wasm` build.

For a walkthrough, see [Run an addon sandboxed in WebAssembly](/bare/how-to/run-an-addon-sandboxed-in-webassembly). For how the sandbox works and what it doesn't stop, see [WebAssembly addons](/bare/explanation/webassembly-addons).
